data.title: TFEB links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
data.authors: Settembre C; Di Malta C; Polito VA; Garcia Arencibia M; Vetrini F; Erdin S; et al.; Ballabio A

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Showed that TFEB drives a coordinated autophagy and lysosomal gene programme during starvation. In this paper TFEB was regulated by ERK2 phosphorylation; its control by mTORC1 at the lysosome was established in later work (SET2012).
data.abstract_excerpt: Autophagy is a cellular catabolic process that relies on the cooperation of autophagosomes and lysosomes. During starvation, the cell expands both compartments to enhance degradation processes. We found that starvation activates a transcriptional program that controls major steps of the autophagic pathway, including autophagosome formation, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, and substrate degradation. The transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master gene for lysosomal biogenesis, coordinated this program by driving expression of autophagy and lysosomal genes.

extracted_findings.effect: TFEB drives a transcriptional program that links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
